reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and date adjustment helpers, but independently implements the daily skip policy in four consumers.

duplication.why: Daily skip decisions recur across shared scheduling, upcoming dates, range dates and budget targets, alongside duplicated filtering and adjustment blocks.

placement.why: Holiday recognition belongs in shared scheduling, but server handlers and budget code also own scheduling policy that should live there.

scope.why: All edits support the requested scheduling changes, their tests or release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several policy implementations and separate scan limits, while the new handler leaves config untyped despite the existing RecurConfig type.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts explicitly requests unadjusted getNextDate results and reconstructs the skip policy; server/schedules/app.ts independently implements that policy in both date handlers.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily non-working-day exclusion appears as array filtering in getNextDate, conditional accumulation in createScheduleList, conditional collection in getUpcomingDates and continue-based filtering in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter; getNextDate gains daily-specific forward filtering, reverse filtering and an adjustment exclusion; createScheduleList, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement the daily policy.
